title: Monday meeting agenda
body:
# Monday meeting

- Review the desktop search prototype.
- Compare keyboard navigation with pointer navigation.
- Leave time for open questions.

The next milestone is a usable source editor, followed by readonly previews.

title: Mountain guide
body:
Trail notes for the north ridge.
Bring a map, warm gloves, and enough water.
The morning route follows the old stone wall before the summit.

title: Meeting
body:
Budget review at 10:00.
Bring the revised estimate.

title: Search roadmap
body:
## First pass

Search every note source, title, and tag.
Keep results in the order returned by the matching engine.

## Later

Compare a body excerpt with a title-only list.
Measure response time while a user types quickly.

title: Evening checklist
body:
Close the windows.
Water the basil.
Check that the automatic backup completed before sleep.
The backup disk sits in the blue drawer.

title: Automatic backup design
body:
# Automatic backups

Create a complete snapshot at a regular interval.
Keep the most recent daily and weekly copies.
A failed copy must not replace the last successful backup.

Restore into a temporary library before replacing the current library.

- chopped onion

- cumin

Finish with lemon juice and parsley.

Ingredients

- eggs
- sugar

Let the cake cool before adding the glaze.

title: Keyboard map
body:
Command-L: focus the search bar.
Command-N: create a note.
Escape: clear the current action.

Literal symbols used in technical notes: ! ^ $ | : " ' .
The sample path is Sources/Browser/NVBrowserSession.m.

title: Punctuation examples
body:
A shell prompt can end in $.
A sentence can start with !important.
The expression ^start.*end$ describes an anchored pattern.
A pipeline uses | between commands.
The phrase "paper kite" appears in this note with quotation marks.

title: Research question
body:
Does fuzzy search help with half-remembered technical terms?

Compare authentication, authorization, and an unrelated abbreviation.
The word synchronization is easy to shorten and easy to mistype.

title: Synchronisation notes
body:
The document uses British spelling: synchronisation.
A fuzzy matcher accepts gaps, but it does not swap characters automatically.
